why: The N/A branch `not an npm project` leaves the DENOMINATOR, and a branch that leaves the denominator is the place where the score climbs with nobody fixing anything — that is how the broken package.json turned 9 of 10 into 6 of 6. While the runner read the exit code, this branch could not be locked: `na` and `passou` both exit 0. The `pass` side is a tree with no package.json at all and has to come out N/A, not `passou`: dependabot and renovate are npm-project configuration, and charging that to a repository that is not npm would be inventing debt. With the mutation `na(...)` → `null`, this side becomes `passou` and the case accuses.
